articles.title: A million people rally for Lula in São Paulo
articles.content_excerpt: Alongside political allies, President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva delivered a speech on São Paulo’s Paulista Avenue to more than a million people who packed the streets this Sunday, October 11. Seeking re-election, Lula highlighted the power of the youth in mobilizing both online and offline and emphasized the importance of young people participating in politics to ensure dignity and rights. “This event is a lesson,” he said. “Either you participate in political life, or it cannot be fixed. You must take responsibility to join the fight while you are young. This country cannot lose its democracy, however flawed it may be.” Lula also recalled the actions of Jair Bolsonaro’s government during the COVID-19 pandemic. articles.title: Can Democrats Flip the House and Senate? The Lever’s David Sirota on Midterm Races To Watch
articles.content_excerpt: The midterm elections are in less than three weeks, on November 3. With Republican majorities in both chambers of Congress on the line, the Trump administration has thrown its time and resources into holding rallies in newly competitive states. We take a look at key Senate races in Georgia, Texas, Michigan and Maine with The Lever ’s David Sirota. Ultimately, says Sirota, election results will hinge on voter turnout. “Will there be that surge of turnout based on how unpopular Trump is and how bad the affordability crisis is?” And, if they win, can Democrats then “deliver” on their promises? articles.title: “Propaganda Show”: IDF Raids Palestinian NGOs in the West Bank Ahead of Israeli Elections
articles.content_excerpt: Israeli forces have raided what they say are the offices of several Palestinian NGOs in the occupied West Bank. Palestinian officials say a child was injured from Israeli gunfire, while others suffered from tear gas inhalation. At least one journalist was reportedly detained in the raids, which come four years after the forced closure of multiple NGOs that the Israeli government designated as “terrorist” organizations. “This is part of the whole propaganda show that this government is actually implementing just before the Israeli election,” says human rights lawyer Sahar Francis. “They just wanted to cause harassment, and this is the main message: the persecution and the collective punishment for the whole Palestinian community.” Francis was formerly the general director at Addameer Prison

articles.title: In the crosshairs of AI
articles.author: Ashley Smith
articles.content_excerpt: I n their mad rush for profit and power, the tech oligarchs have unleashed artificial intelligence (AI) into nearly every corner of life on this planet. Firms are investing billions in data centers, which house the infrastructure to process the enormous amounts of information that power AI. They are also plowing ever more money into research and development. Their hope is that the technology will overcome global capitalism’s slump , which the system has been trapped in since the Great Recession, and trigger a new epoch of expansion. States are incorporating it into their police forces for domestic surveillance as well as their militaries for cyberwarfare and high-tech weapons. articles.title: DR Congo’s deadliest Ebola outbreak kills over 4,200 as armed groups undermine response
articles.author: Pavan Kulkarni
articles.content_excerpt: In less than five months, the fastest-spreading Ebola outbreak in world history has killed at least 4,205 people in the conflict-ridden eastern region of the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) as of October 7. It is the deadliest outbreak in the DRC since the disease was first discovered in the country in 1976, killing nearly one in two of the 8,728 people confirmed to be infected. With treatment still in experimental stages, there is no specifically approved treatment for the particular Bundibugyo strain of the Ebola virus that caused this outbreak, declared on May 15. articles.title: Mali’s army recaptures town of Kidal
articles.author: Nicholas Mwangi
articles.content_excerpt: Mali’s armed forces have recaptured the northern city of Kidal following a large-scale military offensive conducted alongside Russia’s Africa Corps. It is a major development in the government’s efforts to restore state control over territory held by armed groups. articles.title: Ansar Allah has the upper hand in escalating conflict with Saudi Arabia
articles.author: Aseel Saleh
articles.content_excerpt: Three months after Saudi Arabia resumed its aggression against Yemen’s Ansar Allah-led government by attacking Sanaa International Airport in July, the conflict continues to spiral. Saudi-backed forces claimed that they managed to cut off the main road connecting the Red Sea port city of Mokha with the Bab al-Mandeb strait on Monday, October 12, in a bid to reverse Ansar Allah’s major territorial gains along the Red Sea coast. This came after Ansar Allah launched an intensified military operation that resulted in encircling Yemen’s southwestern city of Taiz last week. Taiz has been under the control of the Saudi-backed Yemeni government for roughly the last ten years. As Yemen’s third-largest city, the encirclement of Taiz constitutes a critical development in the country’s armed conflict
source_folders: 06_左派ニュース・社会主義戦略

articles.title: Political crisis in Pakistan deepens with dismissal of PTI-led provincial government
articles.author: Abdul Rahman
articles.content_excerpt: Large-scale protests broke out in different parts of Pakistan’s Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP) province on Monday, October 12, after the federal government dismissed its elected government and imposed the centralized Governor’s rule. The federal government also declared an emergency in 12 out of 40 of KP’s districts, citing a law-and-order situation.
